values.note: FWC: 'Camping is available year-round', but Kowechobe's sites are 'best to access during the dry season (approximately November thru April)'; in the wet season they can be inundated and suit tents, campers or RVs only 'depending on time of year'.

season.source: https://myfwc.com/recreation/lead/dinner-island/camping/ ('Camping is available year-round.') + https://secure.webreserv.com/services/bookingcalendar.do?businessid=dinnerislandranchfl&embedded=y&search=0&avgrid=y&css= ('best to access during the dry season (approximately November thru April)'), read 2026-10-21

values.note: Free camping permit = site reservation, online (FWC's WebReserv page) or by phone to the South Regional Office, Mon-Fri 8-5 only. Permits up to 14 days ahead; at most 14 consecutive days in a month, then 14 days before a new permit. Display the permit by placing a copy in the brochure box at the Hammock Campground. A site left unoccupied 48 hours may be cancelled. One RV and one tent per RV site.

Individuals may apply for a maximum of 14 consecutive days within a given month'; 'All campers must obtain a free permit/site reservation using the online reservation system or by calling'), read 2026-10-21

note: FWC Wildlife Management Area. Kowechobe Camp: open-field sites (40x50 ft each) for tents, campers or RVs; primitive, no amenities. Easy trailer access in dry season (Nov-Apr); may flood and require 4x4 in summer.
summary: FWC still permits camping at Kowechobe Camp: confirmed 20 sites for tents/campers/RVs, free permit-reservation (online WebReserv or phone), year-round camping with dry-season (Nov-Apr) access advised. Added platform/url, fcfs never, 14-day window, 14-night max. Note trimmed of the site count and the free-permit/reservation text the fields now hold. Not stated: hookups (page says 'primitive camp area'), facilities at Kowechobe (the vault toilet is at Hammock Camp), site dimensions.
flags: Wet-season access: FWC says the 20 sites suit tents, campers or RVs 'depending on time of year due to inundated site conditions' and are 'best to access during the dry season (approximately November thru April)'. The note's 'may require 4x4 in summer' is not on FWC's pages (no agency 4WD statement found), so it was left in the note; a human may want to judge whether summer access is realistic for EKKO.
